description: The shape of a log line. Pino on the reference path, spdlog on the fast path, one JSON format. A disagreement between the two is a bug, which is why this is a contract and not a per-implementation setting.
principle: A log line is a structured event with a human sentence attached, not a sentence with fields attached. Tests compare the structure. The sentence is never compared — contracting English prose in two languages achieves nothing and cannot be kept green.
notCopiedFromLegacy: Legacy derives a log4js category per class and per method — 'backend.auth.jwt.JWT.verifyAndDecrypt' is a category. That taxonomy restates the file tree and grows with it. Here the category is a small closed set and the identity of a line is its event id.

envelope.description: Fields every line carries. time, level and msg keep Pino's default names so the reference path needs no custom serializer and the fast path has a fixed target to match.

fields.name: time
fields.description: UTC, see types/Timestamp.json. Pino's default already emits exactly this.

fields.name: event
fields.description: Stable dotted id. This is what tests assert on.

fields.name: msg
fields.description: One human sentence, present tense, no trailing period. Never compared between implementations, never parsed by anything.

fields.name: req
fields.description: Request correlation id. Present on every line emitted while serving a request.

fields.name: usr
fields.description: users.id, never the email and never the gradido_id.

fields.name: err
fields.description: Present when the line reports a failure: { code, name } from contracts/errors.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Event-specific fields, flat, no nesting beyond one level.

rules: No other top-level fields. Anything event-specific goes inside data.
Pino's default base fields pid and hostname must be disabled (base: null). They differ per process and would make two identical runs compare unequal.
No field is ever omitted for being empty except the ones marked optional, and an optional field is absent rather than null.

levels.description: Pino's numeric values. spdlog maps its own levels onto these numbers on output — the number is the contract, the spelling is not.

values.name: warn
values.use: recovered, but someone should know — e.g. an unknown role string from the database

categories.description: Closed set. It reuses the domain vocabulary from AGENTS.md rather than inventing a second taxonomy, so a category is a place in the system, not a place in the source tree. Adding one is a contract change.

values.name: mail
values.description: outbound mail: the session to the relay, and what was sent through it

values.name: dht
values.description: the peer network node: its identity, what it listens on, the calls and announcements that reach it. Not federation, which answers the calls

rules: Lowercase, dot separated, no verbs in the past tense beyond the outcome.
The outcome is the last segment: created, failed, denied, refused, expired, evicted, refreshed, reverted, started, stopped, applied.
An event id never changes once it exists — see AGENTS.md, names are stable forever. To retire one, stop emitting it; do not rename it.
One event id means one shape: the same keys in data every time it is emitted, on both paths.

events.description: Seed set. This grows with the rebuild — an event is contracted when the code that emits it is written, not before.

data.name: impl
data.description: reference | fast

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: The one line where the two implementations may legitimately differ in content: impl says which one is speaking.

data.name: signal
data.description: closed vocabulary: SIGINT, SIGTERM

values.note: The last line of a clean shutdown: connections stopped, database closed, log flushed.

data.name: signal
data.description: closed vocabulary: SIGINT, SIGTERM

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: timeout, error

values.note: The process exits with 1 after this line. timeout means the shutdown outlived its deadline and was cut short, so what it was waiting for did not finish.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: The database did not answer, or answered that it will not: wrong credentials, no such database, no permission. The process exits with 1 after this line.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: no-terminal, not-set-up, config-unwritable, master-seed-invalid

values.note: The process exits with 1 after this line. Distinct from startup.database.failed on purpose: the database answered, what is missing is a setup step nobody has taken. not-set-up is a serving start against a database with no community — serving never asks, it names the `setup` command and stops. no-terminal is that command itself, run where there is nobody to answer it. config-unwritable is that command again, with the answers given and the .env they belong in refused by the file system — nothing was written and nothing was migrated. master-seed-invalid is that command finding a MASTER_SEED that is not 64 hex digits, or one whose named source cannot be read: it is the root of the instance's keys, so setup does not replace it. See db/communities.json.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: unknown_contact, wrong_password, not_verified, deleted

values.note: Never log which of these it was to the client — the response says only that the login failed. The log may be specific; the response may not.
The ignore_and_warn policy of types/RoleNames.json is this line. Both implementations must emit it for the same input.
Hard timeout, SESSION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS.

data.name: capacity
data.description: The configured maximum number of sessions -- the ceiling that was hit, not the number of slots in use.

values.note: The session store reached the ceiling it is configured with and retired its oldest session before that session's hard timeout. The owner's next request is a miss, a signature verification and a fresh session, so this is not an error -- it is the one signal that the store was not allowed to grow to the load it actually has, and warn rather than debug because nobody goes looking for it. Below the ceiling the store grows instead and this line never appears.
Carries err. The path is the route pattern, not the concrete URL — a concrete one leaks ids into the log.

data.name: attempt
data.description: One-based, so attempt 1 is the first try.

data.name: attempts
data.description: How many tries there will be in total.

values.note: One line per failed attempt while waiting for the database at startup. warn, not error: a database that is still starting up is expected, and the line that says it never came is startup.database.failed. The driver's own message goes in msg -- it is not a contracted error code, and it must never carry the connection password.
Carries err. Never the statement text and never the parameters.

data.name: version
data.description: The migration number, which becomes the schema version.

data.name: file
data.description: The migration name, so a line points at something findable.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

data.name: ms
data.description: How long the migration took.

values.note: One line per migration actually applied, at startup. Nothing is logged when the schema is already current: a line per boot saying that nothing changed teaches people to stop reading the log.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: The migration was rolled back in full before this line — both target databases roll DDL back. The process then ends through startup.database.failed, so this line says which step failed and that one says the run is over.

data.name: uuid
data.description: communities.community_uuid — the community's public identity.

data.name: url
data.description: Base URL other communities reach it at.

values.note: Written once, at the first start against a database that has no community. The key pair generated with it is never logged, in whole or in part — see redaction. This is the line an admin looks for when they want to know when the instance was set up.

data.name: version
data.description: The migration that was undone. The database is now at version - 1.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: One down step, and only ever one per run. warn rather than info because a down step is not the inverse of an up step — what it dropped, it dropped with its rows. On a release the run had to be confirmed by naming this migration; how that confirmation is given is each implementation's own business, that it is required is not.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: A down run that did not happen: unconfirmed on a release, confirmed with the wrong name, nothing applied, or a migration with no down step. Which of those is in msg rather than in a field, the way db.connection.failed carries the driver's own message — the process exits with 1 and a person reads the line. Distinct from db.migration.denied, which is about a schema this build cannot run against at all and names where it diverges.

data.name: version
data.description: The applied migration this build cannot account for.

data.name: file
data.description: Its name, as the database recorded it.

data.name: expected
data.description: What this build has at that version, or null when the database is simply ahead.

data.name: db
data.description: postgresql | sqlite

values.note: The database was built by code this build is not, so nothing is applied and the process exits. msg names the migration to go back past and says the branch that applied it is where the down step lives — this one has no down step for a migration it does not have. Distinct from db.migration.failed, where a migration this build does carry was rolled back.

data.name: language
data.description: The Language enum value the account was created with.

values.note: Carries usr with the new users.id. Never the email address — the account is identifiable without carrying personal data into log storage, see redaction.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: address-in-use

values.note: A registration that was answered as if it had succeeded. Carries usr with the id of the member who already holds the address — not of anybody new, because none was created. The answer to the caller says nothing about this; the log is the only place it is visible, which is the point.

data.name: constraint
data.description: Which unique index refused the row, as the driver names it. PostgreSQL gives the constraint; SQLite gives the columns in a sentence and the string is whatever it said.

data.name: attempt
data.description: Which try this was, from 1.

values.note: A generated value -- users.gradido_id or user_contacts.email_verification_code -- was drawn onto one that already exists, and the registration is being tried again with fresh values. Never the address: that is user.registration.denied, which is an answer and not a retry. At 122 and 53 random bits this line is not one an installation should see, which is why it is warn: a run of them is a generator that has stopped being random, and nothing else would ever say so.

data.name: host
data.description: EMAIL_SMTP_HOST. The relay, never the sender — see redaction.

data.name: tls
data.description: closed vocabulary: none, starttls, require, implicit — EMAIL_SMTP_TLS

data.name: auth
data.description: Whether credentials were offered. Which ones is not logged.

values.note: The backend opened a session to the relay at startup, went as far as a mail would — EHLO, the configured TLS upgrade, AUTH where there are credentials — and hung up without sending one. One line per start, and only the backend emits it: it is the role that sends mail.

data.name: host
data.description: EMAIL_SMTP_HOST. The relay, never the sender — see redaction.

data.name: tls
data.description: closed vocabulary: none, starttls, require, implicit — EMAIL_SMTP_TLS

data.name: auth
data.description: Whether credentials were offered. Which ones is not logged.

values.note: The same probe, refused. warn and never fatal: a server whose mail is misconfigured still answers every route that sends none, and the alternative to this line is discovering it on the first registration. The relay's own words go in msg; they are not a contracted error code, and they must never carry the credentials.
EMAIL is false, so nothing was probed and nothing will be sent. Said rather than left silent, because an operator asking why no mail arrives needs one line that answers it.

data.name: nodeKey
data.description: the node's ed25519 public key, hex -- the same on both paths for one MASTER_SEED

data.name: reachability
data.description: public | private -- DHT_REACHABILITY

values.note: Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: complete
data.description: false when the node was left to the process exit: js-libp2p does not finish stopping when the peer closes the same connection at the same moment, so the reference path waits five seconds at most. Always true on the fast path.

values.note: Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: topic-missing, master-seed-missing, master-seed-invalid, delegation-missing, delegation-invalid, delegation-foreign, identity, no-memory, network, poll

values.note: The role stops after this line, and with it the process. The first six say what to configure and each names `setup`; identity, no-memory and poll are the fast path's, network is the node that did not start on either path. Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: address
data.description: a multiaddr the node listens on, or the relayed one a relay took a reservation for

values.note: Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: bytes
data.description: the payload, the frame around it not counted

values.note: Reported, not stored: an announcement is a hint until the handshake. Only one whose delegation verified, from a community not blocked, within the rate per source. Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: protocol
data.description: the operation the call named

values.note: A call with a valid delegation, naming an operation the node takes, within the limits, refused because there is no federation role to hand it to yet. A call naming an operation the node does not take is dropped without an event -- libp2p-ffi drops it inside the module, and the reference path does the same; neither path takes any operation yet. Refusing closes the stream at once, which the caller's failover moves on from. Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: peer, prefix, global -- the scope whose limit had no token left -- or blocked

values.note: Debug: a refused flood is the limits working, and every line of it would be the flood again, in the log. Both paths: fast-servers/dht-node/src/dht_node_server.c and packages/dht-node.
libp2p-ffi's event queue overflowed and dropped this many. Fast path only: the reference path has no queue between itself and js-libp2p.
An event type the role does not handle. Expected, not an error: libp2p-ffi's interface only grows. Fast path only.
A record from libp2p-ffi that does not fit its own length. Fast path only.
libp2p-ffi refused a limit the role set from const.json. Fast path only: the reference path applies its limits itself.
Publishing the provider record under the community key failed, usually for want of peers; it is tried again when the next one connects. Reference path only: libp2p-ffi republishes on its own.

data.name: url
data.description: DHT_BOOTSTRAP_URL, the community whose peer.bootstrap was asked

data.name: peers
data.description: how many of the nodes in the answer, the answering node included, were reached

values.note: Both paths. Asked at start and again every minute while the node has no connection.

data.name: url
data.description: DHT_BOOTSTRAP_URL

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: unreachable, invalid-answer, delegation-invalid

values.note: Both paths. delegation-invalid: self.delegation does not verify, or does not name the key of self.peerId -- the answer is dropped whole, peers included.

redaction.description: Never logged, at any level, in either implementation. Not a policy that can be relaxed by configuration.

never.why: the PHC string carries the salt and the full hash
possession of it is proof of the email

never.what: JWTs, in whole or in part
never.why: a token in a log is a token in every backup of that log
use usr with users.id — the account is identifiable without carrying personal data into log storage

never.what: avatar bytes and any other blob

never.why: it is user input and frequently an email

never.what: concrete request URLs with ids in the path
never.why: log the route pattern; the id belongs in data if it is needed at all

comparison.description: How a contract test decides that both implementations logged the same thing.
rules: Compare: level, cat, event, presence and value of every data key, and err.code when present.
Ignore: msg, time, req, and field order.
A missing event on the fast path is a documented gap, the same as a skipped contract test — not a failure to hide by loosening the comparison.
